subject: Order Form: productization & training carveouts
messages:
From: Maya Singh <maya.singh@foundrytech.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Amit Rao <amit.rao@foundrytech.com>, legal@foundrytech.com
Date: Sun, 18 Oct 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Foundry — initial order form redlines (output & training)

Hi Laura,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Attached are the redlines our legal team marked up for the order form / SOW. High level items we’re asking you to look at before we circulate to procurement:

- Output ownership: We need explicit clarity that Foundry can use model outputs for productization (including embedding into our product UX).
- Training/use of customer data: We request an explicit carveout that allows Foundry to opt-in to use outputs and customer-provided content for further model training.
- Feedback license: Foundry needs a license to use feedback/annotations our users provide to improve our product.

I realize these are material asks. If Redwood can’t grant retraining rights, we’d accept a time-limited license or a metadata/telemetry exception for customer-provided, anonymized datasets. Can we set a 30-minute call early this week to run through options?

Attached: Foundry_OrderForm_Redlines_v3.docx (39 KB); Legal_Summary.pdf (12 KB)

Best,
Maya Singh
Head of Product — Foundry Tech
maya.singh@foundrytech.com

Subject: Re: Foundry — initial order form redlines (output & training)

On Sun, Oct 18, 2026 at 09:14 AM, Maya Singh <maya.singh@foundrytech.com> wrote:
> Thanks again for the demo last week. Attached are the redlines our legal team marked up for the order form / SOW.

Maya — thanks for sending these over and for the clear summary. We can definitely be pragmatic here; happy to run through tradeoffs with Ben and Priyom on our side.

High level reaction from me:
- Output ownership: we typically grant customers rights to outputs for their product features, but we need to preserve Redwood’s ability to operate and improve models. We can discuss a narrowly scoped, perpetual non-exclusive right limited to Foundry’s productization (not redistribution or resale).
- Training/data use: retraining on customer data is sensitive for us. We can offer: (a) an opt-in training program (customer elects, with technical guardrails and SOC2 evidence), or (b) a telemetry/aggregate metrics carveout that allows Foundry to use derived metrics and anonymized aggregates for offline model tuning.
- Feedback license: seems reasonable to grant a feedback license but limited to improvement of Foundry’s product features; we’d ask for an assurance that feedback shared back to Redwood remains subject to our feedback license (simple bilateral protections).

Priyom — tagging you for legal language. Ben — can you commit to a deadline from procurement if we can align on carveouts this week?

I’ll schedule a 30-minute sync tomorrow at 10am PT; if that doesn’t work, propose alternatives.

Thanks,
Laura
Director, Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference.com>

Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 08:23:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Foundry — initial order form redlines (output & training)

Laura / Maya — quick note from the commercial side.

Appreciate the clarity, Maya. Our commercial ask is to avoid an open retrain right — that is a hard sell internally. Possible compromises:
- Grant Foundry a perpetual, non-exclusive right to use outputs within your product (productization) but explicitly exclude the right to retrain Redwood models.
- Offer a paid, opt-in training program (time-boxed) where Foundry can provide datasets under a controlled ingestion process; we can price and SLA that separately.
- For feedback: provide a narrow license for annotations and telemetry that allow Foundry to improve its features, with an obligation not to share raw user content.

If procurement needs a doc to accept, we can prepare a short amendment memo that explains the carveouts and the safeguards (SOC2, ingestion controls, data minimization).

Ben
VP, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.inference.com>
To: Maya Singh <maya.singh@foundrytech.com>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.inference.com>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 11:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Foundry — initial order form redlines (output & training)

Hi all — I reviewed the redlines and sketched suggested language below (high level; we can insert into the order form or a short amendment):

1) Output rights (proposed): 
Foundry is granted a perpetual, worldwide, non-exclusive, non-transferable right to use, reproduce and display Outputs produced by the Services solely to operate and improve Foundry’s internal products and services. Such license does not permit Foundry to distribute, resell, or sublicense Outputs as a standalone model or service.

2) Training & data use (proposed): 
Customer Content and Outputs will not be used by Redwood to train or improve Redwood’s production models unless Customer opts-in via a written, time-limited training program. If Customer opts-in, data ingestion will occur under a controlled process (limited retention, anonymization where feasible, and documented security controls). As an alternative, Redwood may provide aggregate telemetry and derived metrics to assist Customer with offline model tuning.

3) Feedback license (proposed): 
Customer grants Redwood a royalty-free, non-exclusive license to use Feedback (as defined) to operate, maintain and improve the Services, provided that any Feedback that includes Customer Content or Personal Data will be processed subject to the Customer Content protections in the MSA.

4) Evidence & safeguards: Customer may request security evidence (SOC 2 Type II, penetration test summaries) and Redwood will provide standard evidence pursuant to the security exhibit and a reasonable NDA for any sensitive materials.

If Foundry is comfortable with the above we can put the clauses into a short amendment and proceed to DocuSign. If Foundry needs a retraining right beyond an opt-in program, that will require an addendum with pricing and operational controls.

I can draft amendment language this afternoon and post as a link.

— Priyom
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Foundry — initial order form redlines (output & training)

Thanks — that language is helpful and closer to what we need. Two quick clarifications: 

1) For "perpetual" output rights — we need confirmation that "internal products and services" includes SaaS features we surface to our end users (not resale as a model). That is acceptable.
2) For opt-in training: Foundry is prepared to participate in a paid, time-limited training program. We will need the ingestion process and anonymization checklist ahead of time and SOC2 evidence as part of procurement.

If Priyom can send the draft amendment, we’ll review and aim to turn around redlines within 24 hours. If everything checks out we can sign by Nov 1. Please send DocuSign link once we have the amendment.

Best,
Maya
Head of Product — Foundry Tech
